subject: Dual-rate ramp & co-term switch proposal for BlueWave renewal
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Marc Delarue <marc@bluewave.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dual-rate ramp & co-term switch proposal for BlueWave renewal

Marc —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. I pulled together two paths that address BlueWave's goals: predictable unit economics for forecasting, while giving capacity headroom for the Q1 product launch. High level:

1) Dual-rate ramp (preferred):
   - Year 1: lower committed baseline with a higher overage/transaction rate for burst months.
   - Year 2–3: phased baseline increases at pre-agreed milestone dates (50% increase at 12 months, 30% at 24 months) to match expected usage growth.

2) Co-term switch with mid-contract true-up:
   - Sync contract end to calendar-year co-term at a discounted pro-rata adjustment; include a single true-up at month 6 to reconcile prefix cache savings.

I've attached a model (BlueWave_Renewal_Model.xlsx) showing impact on ARR, unit cost per 1M tokens, and estimated monthly invoices under both approaches.

Next steps I recommend:
- You confirm whether the co-term sync is a hard requirement for procurement.
- If dual-rate looks viable, we'll route a draft SOW and pricing sheet to procurement and finance.

Can we block 30 mins next Tue (9/14) to review the workbook?

Thanks,
Sean
Sr. Account Exec — Redwood Inference
(sean.gallagher@redwood.com)

Attachments: BlueWave_Renewal_Model.xlsx

From: Marc Delarue <marc@bluewave.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: BlueWave Renewals <renewals@bluewave.ai>, procurement@bluewave.ai
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 10:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Dual-rate ramp & co-term switch proposal for BlueWave renewal

Sean —

Appreciate the detailed options. Quick answers: procurement prefers co-termination with our FY (Jan 31), but they are open to a mid-contract true-up if it simplifies invoicing. A few things from our side:

- We expect a major traffic spike starting 2028-02 tied to our new feature rollout — that argues for a ramp that preserves latency SLAs rather than aggressive overage exposure.
- Our CFO is pushing for simpler monthly billing (one invoice) and a predictable discount ladder tied to committed baseline.

Can Marissa and your finance team show us a version of the dual-rate that limits overage exposure in months where forecast > 3x baseline? Also want to understand how prefix/KV cache savings factor into the month-6 true-up.

Marc
Head of Engineering — BlueWave Analytics
marc@bluewave.ai

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Marc Delarue <marc@bluewave.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dual-rate ramp & co-term switch proposal for BlueWave renewal

Marc —

Thanks — putting Kimberly (pricing) and Marissa (CS) on this thread. Quick responses:

- We can structure a dual-rate with an "overage-cap" for spike months: if a month exceeds 3x baseline, overage fees are capped at 1.5x the standard overage rate (so cost is predictable while still encouraging a baseline increase).
- The month-6 true-up will reconcile actual KV/prefix cache savings vs projected. In practice that typically reduces net usage by ~8–12% after warm prefixes; we've modeled scenarios at 5%, 10%, and 15% cache lift in the attached pricing workbook (redwood_dual_rate_pricing.xlsx).

I've proposed 9/14 10:00 PT on my calendar; if that doesn't work I can do 9/15 in the morning.

Best,
Sean

---
On Mon, Sep 13, 2027 at 10:02 AM Marc Delarue <marc@bluewave.ai> wrote:
> Sean —
> 
> Appreciate the detailed options...

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marc Delarue <marc@bluewave.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dual-rate ramp & co-term switch proposal for BlueWave renewal

Marc / team —

I ran the numbers on the conservative (5%) and optimistic (15%) cache uplift scenarios. High level:

- If we pick baseline = 65% of current 30-day average, and apply the 6-month true-up with a 10% projected cache lift, BlueWave sees ~7% ARR reduction vs a flat-commit approach in year 1, but total cost volatility drops by ~45% for the first 6 months.
- Suggested commercial: 10% volume discount on baseline committed units + 5% additional discount if co-term to Jan 31 is accepted.
- Procurement note: a co-term PRORATA adjustment (to align end date) will be applied on signed start date and documented in the SOW.

I'm attaching a redlined SOW (SOW_draft_v2.pdf) with the proposed milestone dates and the true-up clause language. If that looks good I can freeze pricing and route to legal for a quick review.

Kimberly
Principal Pricing Analyst — Redwood Inference

From: Marc Delarue <marc@bluewave.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Dual-rate ramp & co-term switch proposal for BlueWave renewal

Team —

This reads well. Procurement confirmed co-term to Jan 31 is required. A couple of asks before we sign:

- Can you include an explicit SLA credit ladder if latency SLOs are missed during the launch window (Feb–Apr 2028)?
- Please confirm the overage-cap math in the workbook with a 4x spike scenario — our traffic model has a non-trivial chance of hitting that.

If you confirm those two items, we can move to an internal approvals queue and expect signature within 10 business days.

Regards,
Marc

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Marc Delarue <marc@bluewave.ai>, BlueWave Renewals <renewals@bluewave.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Sep 2027 14:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dual-rate ramp & co-term switch proposal for BlueWave renewal

Marc —

Thanks — we will:

- Add an SLA credit ladder (Tier 1: 99.9% p95 latency -> 5% credit; Tier 2: 99.5% -> 10% credit) that applies to Feb–Apr 2028 launch window and is scoped to production endpoints only.
- Re-run the overage-cap sheet for a 4x spike and confirm the capped-dollar exposure; updated redwood_dual_rate_pricing.xlsx attached.

I'll drop a follow-up by Monday with the updated workbook and the final SOW ready for signature. Appreciate the quick cadence here — excited to keep BlueWave's rollout smooth.

Best,
Sean
Sr. Account Exec — Redwood Inference
(sean.gallagher@redwood.com)

Attachments: redwood_dual_rate_pricing.xlsx, SOW_draft_v2.pdf
